tasks.short: Conduct design reviews and file the decision

steps.what: Set the slot for regular design reviews
Assemble questions throughout design reviews

loop.input: open question text and known design ids
loop.output: a packet of questions that each cite one design id
loop.check: Every question in the packet cites one design id
loop.stop: One pass, then questions with no design id stay off the packet
loop.why_not_simpler: People name a puzzle in prose instead of a design id, so a fixed filter misses them

steps.what: Conduct design reviews during development
Sign the design reviews decision note
File the signed design reviews note

tasks.design: Open questions for a review sit on the {PROJECT} board with a design id and an owner. A {DOCS} packet lists only questions that cite a design id. The game designer conducts the design reviews in the room and signs one decision. The packet does not replace the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review questions lived in slides and chat, so the room often started without a single list of what was undecided.
tasks.enabler_now: A question can carry a design id and an owner that a packet can list without answering the question.
tasks.still_hard: The review is a conversation. Judging the design in the room does not become a form.
tasks.human_edge: The designer conducts the reviews and decides what changes.
tasks.altitude: Prep is shorter. The reviews stay in the room, and the designer can block a decision that names no design id.

reach.task: Schedule the next review from the signed decision
reach.learn: Which questions were closed and which remain open

evidence.claim: Regular design reviews in a mid-size studio are meetings. The question list is the part with a stable shape, and the judgement in the room is not.
A bounded pass can keep a question that cites a design id. It cannot conduct the review or decide the outcome.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed review decision is filed. The conversation stays in the room.
Input contract: design id, question text, owner role, build id. Producer of the question is the game designer or the producer. Questions with no design id are left off the packet.
The meeting prior is accepted for the review itself. Use the project board's own list before custom code.
unknowns: Who may sign a review decision when the designer is away.
Which design ids the current build actually uses.
research_questions: What share of review questions lack a design id?
How often does the signed decision differ from the packet's open list?

already_counted.description: Conducting the reviews stays in the room
Designer edits the decision note before signing

incremental.description: Keep the question packet headings aligned with new design ids
Producer rebooks a review when the packet is empty

approvals.approved_version: design review decision signed in this session
the same signed design review decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes questions stay as free-text slides, so the packet is thin and the review is unchanged. The high case assumes a clean question list, but conducting the reviews and signing the decision stay manual. Follow-up build work is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain design level documentation and mission outlines

steps.what: Develop the mechanics and the guidelines
Fill level documentation and mission outlines
Check owner and version on the documentation
Sign the level documentation version
File the signed level documentation

tasks.design: The designer enters mechanic id, inputs, fail case and mission id on a {DOCS} form. A template fills the level documentation and the mission outlines from those fields only. Suggested metadata such as owner and version can be wrong, so the designer checks them before signing one version. Only that version is the current page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Level notes were free prose, so a page could not tell a current mechanic id from an old paragraph.
tasks.enabler_now: A mechanic can be stored as an id plus a few fields a template can place under fixed headings.
tasks.still_hard: Writing a true guideline, and deciding what the mechanic should do, stays with the designer.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides the mechanic and signs the documentation.

ambition.what: Update the level documentation when the mechanic changes, not only before a milestone

tasks.altitude: Less time on blank headings. The designer can reject a page that states a mechanic they did not enter.

reach.task: Implement the mechanic from the signed level documentation
reach.learn: Which mechanic ids are current and which mission outlines are unsigned

evidence.claim: Level documentation and mission outlines in a mid-size studio are structured pages plus a design decision. The decision is not a template.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. Here that is limited to owner, version and level id, not the design prose.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed documentation version is filed. Implementing the mechanic is a later task.

Input contract: level id, mechanic id, inputs, fail case, mission id, guideline sentence the designer wrote, owner. Producer is the game designer. An empty guideline stays blank. Suggested owner and version are checked because a prompt fill can be wrong.
Use the document store's own templates and metadata columns before custom code. The meeting prior overstates this task: the time is on the document.
unknowns: Who may sign documentation when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of level pages have a blank fail case?
How often is the suggested owner wrong?

already_counted.description: Writing the mechanic and the guidelines stays with the designer
Checking suggested owner and version stays with the designer

incremental.description: Revise documentation headings when a new mechanic type appears

approvals.approved_version: level documentation version signed in this pass
the same signed level documentation version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes mechanics stay as free prose, so the template fills little and the designer still writes the page. The high case assumes the fields are used, but stating the mechanic, checking metadata and signing stay manual. Implementation time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Document formal design with screenshots and flowcharts

steps.what: File screenshots and sample layouts
Draw gameplay flowcharts as graphical devices
Document formal design aspects from images
Sign the formal design pack
File the signed formal design pack

tasks.design: The artist files a screenshot and a menu layout under a screen id in {DOCS}. The designer draws the gameplay flowchart and names each screen. A pack template places only labelled images under the formal design headings. The designer signs one pack version. Images with no screen id are left out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screenshots and flowcharts sat in folders with no screen id, so a pack could not tell a current menu from an old picture.
tasks.enabler_now: An image file can carry a screen id and a caption the designer wrote, which a pack can place by that id.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the visual and drawing the flowchart are design acts. A template does not invent a screen.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides which screenshots and flowcharts belong in the formal design.
tasks.altitude: Assembly of the pack is shorter. The designer still draws the flowchart and can drop an image with no screen id.

reach.task: Replace a screenshot the designer marked out of date
reach.learn: Which screen ids are in the signed formal pack

evidence.claim: Formal design packs in a mid-size studio are made of screenshots, menu layouts and flowcharts a person draws. Placing labelled images under headings is the part with a stable shape.
A template can place an image that already has a screen id. It cannot draw a flowchart or decide the visual style.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed formal pack is filed. Drawing the flowchart stays manual.

Input contract: screen id, image file, caption the designer or artist wrote, flowchart file, design version. Producer of images is the artist. Producer of the flowchart is the game designer. Images with no screen id are excluded by rule.
Use the document store's own templates before custom code. The meeting prior does not fit this task: the time is on the documents and the drawing tool.
unknowns: Whether screen ids are stable across menu changes.
Who may sign the pack when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of screenshots arrive with no screen id?
How often is a flowchart redrawn after the pack is signed?

already_counted.description: Drawing the flowcharts stays with the designer
Designer drops a misplaced image before signing

incremental.description: Update pack headings when a new screen type appears
Artist replaces screenshots the pack rejected for a missing screen id

approvals.approved_version: formal design pack signed in this pass
the same signed formal design pack

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most images have no screen id, so the pack is assembled by hand and drawing is unchanged. The high case assumes labelled images drop into headings, but drawing flowcharts and signing the pack stay manual. New art is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give design feedback to colleagues and file it

steps.what: List features the feedback will cover
Provide feedback to designers and colleagues
Respond on the design features
Draft feedback regarding design features
Sign the feedback note for colleagues
File the signed feedback for colleagues

tasks.design: The designer lists the feature id and the point they want to make in {DOCS} before the conversation. The conversation with designers and other colleagues stays in the room. A note afterwards quotes only those points. The designer signs the note. It does not invent feedback that was not said.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback was spoken and then retyped from memory, so the written note often drifted from the point.
tasks.enabler_now: A point can be stored as a feature id plus a sentence the designer wrote, which a note can quote.
tasks.still_hard: How to say it, and whether the feature should change, is a conversation and a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides the feedback and how direct to be with colleagues.
tasks.altitude: The conversation stays. Writing the note takes less reconstruction, and the designer can strike a sentence they did not say.

reach.task: Adjust the feature the feedback names
reach.learn: Which points were signed and which were only discussed

evidence.claim: Feedback to colleagues in a mid-size studio is a conversation. A short note that quotes points the designer already wrote is the part with a stable shape.
A template can quote a sentence the designer listed against a feature id. It should not soften, expand or invent the feedback.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed feedback note is filed. The conversation is the centre of the task.

Input contract: feature id, point text the designer wrote, colleague role, date. Producer is the game designer. If no point was written, the note stays empty and the designer types it after the meeting.
The meeting prior is accepted. Use the document store's own template before custom code.
unknowns: Who the colleagues are on a given feature.
Who may sign the note when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of feedback notes add a point that was not said in the room?
How often is the feature id missing?

already_counted.description: Giving the feedback stays a conversation
Designer strikes a sentence they did not say

incremental.description: Keep the feedback note headings aligned with feature ids

approvals.approved_version: feedback note signed after this conversation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes points are not written down before the conversation, so the note is still typed by hand and the conversation is unchanged. The high case assumes the note only quotes listed points, but giving the feedback and signing stay manual. The colleague's later changes are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The designer still runs the reviews and the feedback conversations, and spends less of the week on blank documentation pages and unlabelled screenshots.
reach: Programmers build from a signed level document instead of an old chat thread.
Artists see which screenshot is in the current formal pack and which screen id is out of date.
skills_to_grow: Write a mechanic as an id, inputs, a fail case and a player-visible result before the page is filled.
Label a screenshot with the screen id it shows before it enters a pack.
Keep a design review as a conversation, and the decision as a short signed note.
role.ambitious_version: Every review opens on a current level document, a labelled formal pack and a decision note from the last review.
